legend: It's dinner time, and Busy Beaver has to feed his baby beavers.

Busy Beaver has N%%ZSMJ0%% baby beavers, numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to N%%ZSMJ2%%. The older baby beavers have bigger indices than the younger ones; for example, beaver 1%%ZSMJ3%% is the youngest while beaver N%%ZSMJ4%% is the oldest.

Busy Beaver also has 2N%%ZSMJ5%% dishes, which are numbered from 1%%ZSMJ6%% to 2N%%ZSMJ7%%. If a beaver eats dish i%%ZSMJ8%%, its satisfaction will increase by i%%ZSMJ9%%. Each beaver starts with 0%%ZSMJ10%% satisfaction.
Now, Busy Beaver wants to distribute the dishes amongst his baby beavers subject to the following constraints:
Each beaver should get exactly two dishes.

After all dishes are consumed, older beavers should have at least as much satisfaction as younger beavers. Formally, for any i,j%%ZSMJ11%% with 1≤i<j≤N%%ZSMJ12%%, beaver i%%ZSMJ13%%'s satisfaction should not exceed beaver j%%ZSMJ14%%'s satisfaction.
The parity of beaver i%%ZSMJ15%%'s satisfaction should be ci%%ZSMJ16%% (odd or even).
Determine if there exists a way to feed all N%%ZSMJ17%% beavers that respects these constraints. Additionally, if the task is possible, print any valid assignment of dishes to beavers.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer T%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤T≤104%%ZSMJ19%%) — the number of test cases. The description of each test case follows.
The first line of each test case contains an integer N%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤N≤105%%ZSMJ21%%) — the number of baby beavers.

The second line of each test case contains a string c%%ZSMJ22%% of length N%%ZSMJ23%%, where each of the characters ci%%ZSMJ24%% is either 'O' or 'E'. If ci%%ZSMJ25%% is 'O', the beaver i%%ZSMJ26%% wants its satisfaction to be an odd number. If ci%%ZSMJ27%% is 'E', the beaver i%%ZSMJ28%% wants its satisfaction to be an even number.
It is guaranteed that the sum of N%%ZSMJ29%% across all test cases is no more than 105%%ZSMJ30%%.
output: For each test case, if it is possible to feed the beavers, output "YES" (without quotes) on the first line. Next, print N%%ZSMJ31%% lines describing how to feed each beaver. The i%%ZSMJ32%%-th of these lines should contain two integers, which denote the indices of the two dishes that will be given to beaver i%%ZSMJ33%%.
If it is impossible to feed the beavers, output "NO" (without quotes).
You can output "YES" and "NO" in any case (for example, strings "yES", "yes" and "Yes" will be recognized as a positive response).
There are two subtasks for this problem.
(25%%ZSMJ34%% points): For each test case, the string c%%ZSMJ35%% either only consists of 'O's or only consists of 'E's.
note: In the first test case, one possible way to feed the beavers is as follows:
Feed dishes 2%%ZSMJ37%% and 3%%ZSMJ38%% to beaver 1%%ZSMJ39%%. Beaver 1%%ZSMJ40%% gains satisfaction of 5%%ZSMJ41%%, which is odd.
Feed dishes 5%%ZSMJ42%% and 1%%ZSMJ43%% to beaver 2%%ZSMJ44%%. Beaver 2%%ZSMJ45%% gains satisfaction of 6%%ZSMJ46%%, which is even.
Feed dishes 4%%ZSMJ47%% and 8%%ZSMJ48%% to beaver 3%%ZSMJ49%%. Beaver 3%%ZSMJ50%% gains satisfaction of 12%%ZSMJ51%%, which is even.
Feed dishes 7%%ZSMJ52%% and 6%%ZSMJ53%% to beaver 4%%ZSMJ54%%. Beaver 4%%ZSMJ55%% gains satisfaction of 13%%ZSMJ56%%, which is odd.
The satisfaction of the four beavers in increasing order of age are [5,6,12,13]%%ZSMJ57%%. It can be checked that this assignment satisfies the conditions.
In the second test case, it can be shown that the task is impossible.
